clue.text: Go ahead star

definitions.meaning: to go ahead of the others in a race is to get in front
to star in a show is to play the principal role

explanation.surface: An instruction urging a celebrity to proceed.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses mean moving into first place: in front of a field, or in the principal part of a production.

clue.text: A climbing French wall plant

indicators.note: in a down entry, climbing means the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: mur is the French word for wall

explanation.surface: A climbing plant growing up a wall in France.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'climbing' means reading upwards, so the French word is turned round. ARUM lilies are often called cuckoo-pint in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: The arum is a lily-like flowering species, a type of plant.

clue.text: Attack the copper with acid

parts.note: reads like an assault on a policeman, but describes biting a design into a copper plate with acid

explanation.surface: A violent assault on a police officer using acid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' looks like slang for a police officer; here it is the metal of an engraver's plate.
explanation.definitionFit: Engravers cut designs into metal plates by letting acid eat away the exposed surface.

clue.text: He toils in far from friendly fashion

indicators.note: 'in ... fashion' says the letters of He toils are fashioned into a new order

explanation.surface: A man labours in a very unfriendly way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in ... fashion' frames the anagram of HE TOILS.
explanation.definitionFit: Hostility is enmity, the opposite of warmth towards someone.

clue.text: Swing till dizzy

indicators.note: dizzy suggests the letters of till spinning into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone swings around until feeling giddy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dizzy' rearranges TILL.
explanation.definitionFit: A swing in music or speech is a rhythmic, lively cadence.

clue.text: Chemical one keeps in school

indicators.note: keeps means holds within it, so one word surrounds the other

parts.note: an ace is the one in a pack of cards
Eton is the famous English public school

explanation.surface: A chemical substance stored inside a school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one' suggests the number or I; here it is the playing card. Eton is the English private school near Windsor.
explanation.definitionFit: Acetone is a solvent used in nail-varnish remover, an organic compound.

clue.text: Pupil's knowledgeable, gets academic award

parts.note: a scholar is a pupil or student, here with the possessive s
hip is slang for well-informed, in the know

explanation.surface: A clever pupil wins a prize.
explanation.definitionFit: A grant of money awarded for academic merit to fund study.

clue.text: Not even sufficient, strange as it may seem

parts.note: odd numbers are not even, so oddly means in a not-even way
enough means sufficient

explanation.surface: A complaint that a quantity is uneven and short, which is surprising.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom introducing something surprising or paradoxical.

clue.text: Russian missile to move along swiftly

definitions.meaning: clouds ... when driven fast across the sky

explanation.surface: A Russian rocket races along.
explanation.definitionFit: A Soviet weapon's NATO name, and a verb for racing along before the wind.

clue.text: Alert pirate looks mercurial

parts.note: quick means sharp or alert
Long John Silver is the pirate in Treasure Island

explanation.surface: A watchful buccaneer appears changeable.
explanation.definitionFit: Quicksilver is the old name for mercury, and as an adjective means changeable or volatile.

clue.text: One among many returning to work

indicators.note: returning means the assembled letters are read backwards
among means placed within the other word

parts.note: a lot means many
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: One of a crowd going back to their job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'among' puts I inside LOT to make LIOT; 'returning' turns that round.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard labour or toil is strenuous, laborious exertion.

clue.text: The done thing

parts.note: the idiom for proper etiquette, read literally as a thing that has been accomplished

explanation.surface: The socially correct way to behave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The done thing' normally means good manners; read literally, it is something you have done.
explanation.definitionFit: An accomplishment is something successfully carried out.

clue.text: Unmatched French writer finishes miscellaneous articles

parts.note: an odd sock is unmatched
George Sand was the French novelist
ends means finishes

explanation.surface: A peculiar French author completes a collection of assorted essays.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means assorted leftover bits and pieces.

clue.text: The French mark all dice differently

indicators.note: differently means the letters of all and dice are arranged another way

explanation.surface: A French scorekeeper rolls dice in various ways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'differently' rearranges ALL plus DICE.
explanation.definitionFit: The hook under a c, as in garçon, is a diacritic used in French spelling.

clue.text: Gangsters — a case for some anxiety

indicators.note: Gangsters encases a run of letters, holding some of them inside

explanation.surface: Mobsters are a worrying matter.
explanation.walkthrough: The outer G and ERS of 'Gangsters' form the case round the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Angst is a German loanword for deep dread or unease.

clue.text: I meant having a change to cheer things up

indicators.note: having a change says the letters of I meant, with a, are altered into a different order

explanation.surface: Someone clarifies their remark to lighten the mood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having ... change' rearranges I MEANT plus A.
explanation.definitionFit: To enliven is to bring life and energy to a situation.

clue.text: A searching examination, by all accounts

definitions.text: A searching examination, by all accounts

parts.words: A searching examination, by all accounts
parts.note: 'by all accounts' seems to mean reportedly, but is an inspection carried out across all the financial records

explanation.surface: A thorough investigation, so people say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by all accounts' usually means 'reportedly'; here it is literal: an inspection of the books.
explanation.definitionFit: An official inspection of a firm's financial records by an accountant.

clue.text: Provide proper directions first

indicators.note: first places the directions before the other piece

parts.note: E and N are the compass points east and north
due means proper or fitting, as in due care

explanation.surface: An instruction to supply suitable guidance at the outset.
explanation.definitionFit: To endue is to endow or furnish someone with a quality.

clue.text: This month in an abbreviated way

parts.words: This month in an abbreviated way
parts.note: describes the short form of the old business-letter word for the current month

explanation.surface: A shorthand way of referring to the present month.
explanation.walkthrough: Old business letters wrote 'the 5th inst.' for the 5th of this month, short for instant.
explanation.definitionFit: Inst. abbreviates instant, the commercial term for the current month.

clue.text: Ducks to see in European capital

parts.note: in cricket a duck is a score of nothing, so ducks are zeros, Os
lo is an archaic word for see or behold

explanation.surface: Ducks go sightseeing in a European city.
explanation.walkthrough: A duck is a score of nought in cricket, so ducks are O's.
explanation.definitionFit: Oslo is the capital city of Norway.

clue.text: Meat jelly made with a non-eastern spice

indicators.note: non-eastern means E, the abbreviation for eastern, is removed

explanation.surface: A savoury jelly flavoured with a spice not from the Orient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'non-eastern' drops the E from SPICE, leaving SPIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Aspic is a savoury gelatine made from meat stock.

clue.text: What does father make of the RAF?

definitions.text: What does father make of the RAF?

parts.words: What does father make of the RAF?
parts.note: seems to ask a parent's opinion of the air force, but asks what the word father is in relation to the letters of the RAF

explanation.surface: Asking a dad what he thinks of the air force.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of THE RAF rearrange to FATHER, so father is this of them.
explanation.definitionFit: A word formed by rearranging the letters of another is a rearrangement of this kind.

clue.text: Fruit for the shy

parts.note: seems to offer food to timid people, but names the target at a fairground throwing stall

explanation.surface: A gift of fruit for timid people.
explanation.walkthrough: A coconut shy is a British fairground stall where you throw balls to knock coconuts off posts; 'shy' is not timid.
explanation.definitionFit: A large hard-shelled nut of a palm, the prize at a fairground stall.

clue.text: He gets French wine at a minimal charge

parts.note: vin is the French word for wine
a cent is the smallest coin, so a minimal price

explanation.surface: A man buys French wine very cheaply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He' is the definition: a man's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Vincent is a man's given name, as for the painter van Gogh.

clue.text: Jolly good for bad driving

definitions.meaning: in golf, ... is hitting the ball above its centre, a poor drive

explanation.surface: Praise that sounds ironic about a reckless motorist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'driving' suggests cars; it is a golf drive, where topping the ball sends it skidding along the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Old British slang for splendid, and the golf fault of striking the ball's upper half.

clue.text: Fitting combination of middle English and French

parts.note: et is French for and

explanation.surface: A suitable blend of medieval English and French.
explanation.definitionFit: Meet is an archaic word for suitable or proper.

clue.text: Is the French one ringed in the main?

parts.note: taken as written
le is the French for the

explanation.surface: Asking whether a French item is encircled in the chief part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the main' is the open sea, which rings an island.
explanation.definitionFit: An island is land surrounded by sea, poetically called the main.

clue.text: One in jail killed his brother

indicators.note: in means placed within the other word

parts.note: can is slang for prison
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A prisoner who murdered his sibling.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition stands for 'he who killed his brother'.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis, Cain murdered Abel, his sibling.

clue.text: Scheme for lopping a tree?

indicators.note: lopping means cutting off the last letter of the tree

parts.note: the plane is a common tree

explanation.surface: A plan for pruning a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lopping' cuts the final E from PLANE.
explanation.definitionFit: A scheme is a design or proposed method of action.

clue.text: Now fit and decent

parts.note: the present is now
able means fit or capable

explanation.surface: Someone is currently healthy and respectable.
explanation.definitionFit: Decent here means fit to be seen, respectable in appearance.

clue.text: Seems agreeable but doesn't remain attentive

definitions.meaning: one who assents shows agreement with a movement of the head
to drift off to sleep momentarily

explanation.surface: Someone who looks compliant but drifts off.
explanation.definitionFit: Both describe dipping the head: in assent, or when dozing off.

clue.text: Being rude, I am short and to the point

parts.note: I'm is the short form of I am
pertinent means relevant, to the point

explanation.surface: Someone excuses their rudeness by being brief and direct.
explanation.definitionFit: Impertinent means cheeky or insolent.
